clue.text: Singer might need this immediately before November

blocks.note: first meaning: a microphone, informally
second meaning: the code word that comes just ahead of November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A performer gets something ready just ahead of a gig in November.
explanation.walkthrough: The radio alphabet runs ... Lima, Mike, November, Oscar ..., so the letter word just before November is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer uses a microphone, informally shortened, and the same word is the NATO alphabet code for the letter M.

clue.text: A tramp is chewing smoked beef

indicators.note: chewing mashes things up, so the preceding letters get mangled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A vagrant munches on a deli sandwich filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, cured and smoked beef, served sliced in delicatessens.

clue.text: Bullet — I replaced a charge

indicators.note: the letter I is put in where another vowel stood, swapping one letter for another

blocks.note: the wordplay needs the animal word, the first four letters of this word
the letter itself, taking the place of U

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a round of ammunition was swapped out at some cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay works only on BULL with its U changed to I; the printed 'Bullet' carries two letters the parse cannot use, apparently a slip in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is an invoice or statement of money owed, so it is a charge to be paid.

clue.text: Ancestor responsible for golfer's warning to Rupert, perhaps

blocks.note: the cry a golfer shouts to warn of an incoming ball
joins the warning to the one receiving it
Rupert Bear is a long-running British children's comic-strip character, so he is an example of a bear

explanation.surface: A forebear is blamed for a golfer yelling a warning at someone called Rupert.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a famous British cartoon bear in checked trousers, hence 'perhaps' marking him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is a person from whom one is descended, the same relation as an ancestor.

clue.text: Badger caught other bats outside

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the word before it is jumbled up
the jumbled word sits outside, wrapping around the cricket abbreviation

blocks.note: used as written before being jumbled
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A badger is snared while some other animals flutter round about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to pester; 'bats' is not the animal either.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or harass someone insistently, the same as to badger them.

clue.text: A word to be reckoned with?

definitions.text: A word to be reckoned with?

blocks.clueFragment: A word to be reckoned with?
blocks.note: surface reading: an influential word, as in a force to be reckoned with
setter's reading: a word that means able to be reckoned, that is, computed

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a force to be reckoned with' suggests something formidable; read literally, the word wanted simply means 'able to be reckoned' in the counting sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to compute, so something that can be reckoned is something that can be worked out numerically.

clue.text: Old French inhabitant of London or Manchester

indicators.note: something that inhabits the following words lives inside them, spanning their letters

blocks.note: running from the last letter of London across or into Manchester

explanation.surface: A historic Frenchman is said to live in one of two big English cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans were medieval French people from Normandy, and their dialect is a form of Old French.

clue.text: Try to get attention of rider on the way

definitions.note: an interjection used to do this, not a verb

blocks.note: a postscript is a rider added to a letter, abbreviated PS
in a down answer, 'on' puts the first piece above the second
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone tries to catch a horse rider's eye as they pass along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horse or bike, but it is an addition to a document, the postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissing sound people make to attract someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Following air crash, question one foreign national

indicators.note: a crash smashes things to pieces, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: used as written before rearranging
Q is the standard abbreviation for question
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: After a plane crash, investigators interview a passenger from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a citizen of Iraq, a national of a country other than Britain from the setter's view.

clue.text: Directors taking musical high ground

blocks.note: an opera is a musical drama
tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Film or stage directors stake out the moral high ground over a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators are people who run or manage something, just as directors control a business or machine.

clue.text: Text "lemon squash" for commendation

indicators.note: squashing something crushes it out of shape, so the letters in front get reshaped

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: Someone praises a drink by sending a message naming it lemon squash.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemon squash is a British fruit cordial diluted with water, so 'squash' reads as part of a drink's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Extolment is the act of extolling, praising highly, which is what commendation means.

clue.text: Space traveller to arrive on time

blocks.note: to come is to arrive
in an across answer, the next piece follows
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An astronaut is expected to land punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body orbiting the sun, so it literally travels through space.

clue.text: Drug fish (a whopper)

blocks.note: char is a fish of the trout family
a whopper is a huge lie

explanation.surface: An angler's tale of an enormous fish, perhaps fuelled by narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whopper' tempts a big-fish reading; it is the fib an angler tells.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is British slang for cocaine, from the C of its initial.

clue.text: Ex-President working away from rock outcrop

indicators.note: when something goes away from a word, those letters leave it

blocks.note: Bill Clinton, former US President
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A retired leader is out walking somewhere away from a rocky crag.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the 'working' word from the end of the President's surname leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clint is a flat block of exposed limestone between fissures in limestone pavement, a geological term for a rock outcrop.

clue.text: Trade lies, though result is large shiner!

indicators.note: to trade is to exchange, so the letters swap places with each other

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: Swapping fibs leads to someone getting a big black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A shiner is slang for a black eye, which the surface wants; here it is anything that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse is a tower with a powerful lamp, so it is a very big thing that shines.

clue.text: Decrees that runners hold nothing back

indicators.note: going back means the word for nothing is read in the opposite direction
to hold something is to have it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a runner is a long narrow rug laid in a hall or on stairs
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Official orders say that athletes must not hold back in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes, but these are long strips of carpet; the reversed nought sits between their second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulings are official decisions issued by an authority, which is what decrees are.

clue.text: Rent left in small pit

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the letter goes into the hole word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
L is the abbreviation for left
used as written

explanation.surface: Rent money has been left behind in a little hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as a payment, but it is the past tense of rend: torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or rip in fabric, and a split is the same kind of break.

clue.text: Chemical company no good at producing sugar coating

blocks.note: Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British chemicals giant
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A chemicals firm turns out to be poor at making a sugary glaze.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was Britain's big chemicals company for most of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sweet glaze of sugar spread over cakes, a sugar coating.

clue.text: Push leader away from shaft

indicators.note: with the leader away, the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to prod is to push or poke

explanation.surface: Someone shoves a boss away from a mineshaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a long thin bar, which is one meaning of shaft, as in the shaft of a spear.

clue.text: Wrong direction? I lost belief

indicators.note: the letter that is lost drops out of the word
something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged correctly

blocks.note: used as written
the letter to be removed once

explanation.surface: Having taken a wrong turn, someone loses their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one I out of the nine-letter word, then shuffle the remaining eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a set of teachings held to be true, a body of belief.

clue.text: 3 almost filled with a second second plant

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the referenced answer loses its last letter
being filled with something means holding it inside, so letters go in

blocks.note: the answer to 3 down
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A cross-reference teases with a doubled word before naming a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: BILL shortened to BIL holds A and S; the clue prints 'second' twice, and only one is needed by the wordplay, so the other is surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb, a plant grown for cooking.

clue.text: Precise remedy

blocks.note: first meaning: exact, particular
second meaning: a medicine aimed at one particular disease

explanation.surface: An exact cure is being sought.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific as an adjective means exact; as a noun it is a medicine targeting a particular ailment.

clue.text: Note insect on unknown sort of grass

blocks.note: ti (or te) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a moth is an insect
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A musical note about an insect sitting on an unidentified kind of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is a perennial meadow grass grown widely for hay.

clue.text: Island flower growing with this

definitions.note: describes the stuff something grows with, a noun

blocks.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: An island bloom thrives when fed with this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river here, the thing that flows; the Ure runs through North Yorkshire. The whole clue also describes the answer's use.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure is animal dung spread as fertiliser, what plants are grown with.

clue.text: Young climber says yes to pudding

blocks.note: an informal form of yes
a pie is a kind of pudding or dessert

explanation.surface: A young mountaineer agrees to dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a social climber, someone ambitious.
explanation.definitionFit: A yuppie is a young urban professional, an ambitious young social and career climber.

clue.text: Kind of long stick found outside

indicators.note: a word found outside surrounds the other piece, wrapping around it

blocks.note: to cement is to stick together
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A sort of lengthy rod is discovered out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'sort of', but 'Kind' is the definition (gentle, merciful) and 'of' just joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful or lenient, a sense close to kind.

clue.text: North American bird finds company after a month

blocks.note: Jun is the abbreviation for June
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a flock of a New World bird one month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the company piece behind the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A junco is a small grey sparrow-like finch found across North America.

clue.text: Raise part of hand, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: to lift, as with a car tool
second meaning: a playing card that might be among those held in a card hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of hand' suggests a finger; the hand is the set of cards a player holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack up is to lift with a jack, and the jack or knave is a court card that might be dealt to a player.

clue.text: Bird wants ripe green nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the preceding letters go wildly out of order

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A bird craves nuts that are ready to eat yet still unripe in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like the bird's food but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine is a falcon, the fastest-diving bird of prey.

clue.text: Produce less tax — it's character building

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the answer, a noun

indicators.note: less means minus, so the following word is taken away

blocks.note: to generate is to produce
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: Paying less tax is said to build moral fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character building' sounds like improving someone's personality; in genetics a character is an inherited trait.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene is a unit of heredity that determines inherited traits, which biologists call characters.

clue.text: Stained second half first, creating disturbance

indicators.note: putting the back half at the front rotates the word around its midpoint

blocks.note: stained with colour means dyed

explanation.surface: A stained second-half shirt causes trouble in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling counter-current in water or air, a disturbance in the flow.

clue.text: Chair isn't repaired for believer

indicators.note: a repaired item has been put back together, here with its letters in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A broken chair has not been fixed for a churchgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian is a follower of the faith of Christ, a religious believer.

clue.text: New Aida production for maiden in spring

indicators.note: a new production of a work restages it, so the letters are re-staged in another order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the Verdi opera's name, used as written

explanation.surface: A fresh staging of Verdi's opera calls for a young woman to appear in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season but means a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a naiad is a nymph living in a spring, river or fountain.
